set.hook: Fatih Tutak's Bomonti dining room: one long micro-seasonal tasting, built from Anatolia's regions.
set.why: Tutak cooked his way through Bangkok, Tokyo and Copenhagen before coming home in 2019 to open TURK on a quiet Bomonti street. The menu is one long tasting that the house asks you to allow about 200 minutes for, with the first bites served in the lounge before you sit. Men need a collar and long trousers. In December 2025 the MICHELIN Guide Türkiye kept its two Stars and named it among the 2026 Green Star kitchens.
set.hours: Dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday; closed Sunday and Monday per several listings. Start time is given as 18:30 or 19:00 - call ahead
set.price_range: ₺₺₺₺ - tasting menu only. The house reservation page prices it per guest, but extracts conflict (19,900 TL reported from the page on 12 Aug 2026; 14,500 TL and 23,900 TL also seen, plus a per-guest deposit) - check turkft.com/reservation before booking

set.hook: Mehmet Gürs's dining room and terrace on top of The Marmara Pera, cooking from Anatolian producers.
set.why: Mikla opened in October 2005 on the top two floors of The Marmara Pera, and in 2012 Gürs gave its cooking a name: the New Anatolian Kitchen, built on Turkish producers and regional ingredients rather than imported luxury. MICHELIN gave it a Star in its first Istanbul selection in October 2022, and it kept it in the 2026 Türkiye edition. Arrive before sunset and ask for a table by the glass, facing the Golden Horn and the old city.

set.hook: Maksut Aşkar's Anatolian tasting menus on the top floor of SALT Galata, in the old Ottoman Bank.
set.why: Aşkar opened Neolokal in 2014 inside SALT Galata, the cultural centre that occupies the former Ottoman Bank headquarters on Bankalar Caddesi, so you reach dinner through a library and exhibition building rather than a hotel lobby. MICHELIN gave it a Star and a Green Star in the first Istanbul selection in 2022. In the 2026 edition the guide's Sommelier Award went to its sommelier, Ersin Topkara, a rare honour for a Turkish wine list.

set.hook: Mustafa Otar's open-fire counter in the Passage de Petits Champs: Imroz lamb, Çanakkale fish, house bottarga.
set.why: Mustafa Otar opened Kontuar in January 2026, and the Hürriyet Daily News reviewer described it as the fulfilment of a dream he had held since he was a student. The room is built around a single open fire inside a 19th-century Pera arcade. The menu moves with what producers send: lamb from Imroz (Gökçeada), line-caught fish from Çanakkale and bottarga cured by hand. Listings name turbot with pil pil sauce, salted mackerel and glazed beef tongue.
set.caveat: Hours conflict: a directory gives Monday-Saturday, kitchen 18:00-23:30 with the bar to 01:00, closed Sunday; another claim has Tuesday-Saturday to 22:30. A directory puts the average spend near 4,500 TRY a head (unverified). No verified coordinate: aim for No:67A inside the passage.

set.hook: An all-day Asmalımescit kitchen from three partners, one of them Neolokal's Maksut Aşkar.
set.why: Todos los días is Spanish for every day, and that is the plan: one kitchen running from breakfast to late dinner at Meşrutiyet 67, next door to Kontuar. Esen Hünal and Maksut Aşkar lead the food and Erim Leblebicioğlu the business, a three-way partnership that is rare in a city where star chefs usually work alone. The card runs from egg hummus in the morning to schnitzel with potato salad and gochujang bucatini at night.

set.hook: Two European-trained chefs on the Caddebostan shore road, cooking offal and street food with French technique.
set.why: Kaan Sakarya and Derin Arıbaş cooked in European kitchens before opening on Operatör Cemil Topuzlu Caddesi, the shore road one block from Bağdat Caddesi. MICHELIN's inspectors describe a card that crosses European and Turkish habits with a street-food edge, and pick out a brioche with tomato jam and stracciatella and a pan con tomate laid with anchovies. The offal plates follow the same idea: humble cuts, exact technique, a small room.

set.hook: Uluç Sakarya's market-led daily menu, now on Bağdat Caddesi; a 2026 Bib Gourmand.
set.why: Sakarya shops at the fish and vegetable markets every morning and writes the menu from what he finds, so the card changes daily. He came to cooking late, after a career in textiles, and opened Nazende in 2019 on Plaj Yolu Sokak. In March 2026 Mutfak Magazin reported the restaurant open again at its new address, Bağdat Caddesi 345A, in the Kınayman block. Reviewers single out the grilled squid and the offal plates.

set.hook: A small family meyhane on Asmalımescit Caddesi: cold meze, Black Sea anchovy and rakı, evenings only.
set.why: The same family has worked this room for about a quarter of a century, father, mother, son and daughter, by Fatih Tutak's account to the BBC. The tables sit close and the meze comes to you: stuffed mussels, Armenian topik made from chickpea and onion, and in winter hamsi, the Black Sea anchovy. Reviews from spring 2026 split on value, praising the produce and the welcome while some found the portions small for the bill.

set.hook: A Trabzon family's fish house on the Rumeli Kavağı quay, known for turbot cooked slowly in a tandır.
set.why: Kahraman Altun's grandfather rowed from Trabzon during the First World War, and the family has cooked fish ever since; Altun opened this house on the Rumeli Kavağı quay in 1996 after 18 years at other stoves. The MICHELIN Guide lists it and names the grilled turbot the house speciality, with fish kokoreç beside it. The public ferry from Eminönü takes about one hour forty minutes, so the boat ride becomes part of lunch.

set.hook: Türev Uludağ's Adana grill on the Arnavutköy shore road, cooking Çukurova-style over wood and charcoal.
set.why: TAM stands for Türev'in Adana Mutfağı, Türev's Adana kitchen, and the chef is Adana-born. Food writers call it a Çukurova ocakbaşı: kebabs, köfte and lamb chops over wood and charcoal, with the grill in front of you. Diners name the hand-minced kıyma kebab, çöp şiş, içli köfte cooked in the embers and kaymaklı kadayıf to finish. On Friday and Saturday nights the two floors turn loud, often with arabesque music.

set.hook: A Karaköy grill reborn in Gümüşsuyu under a glass roof, the old city skyline across the water.
set.why: Mesai was Gen Group's first brand, and it came back at İnönü Caddesi 26 in Gümüşsuyu at the end of 2025. Chef Ali Karababa keeps the cooking simple and built around fire, while the room plays as a night out with a bar and a long table. Forbes Türkiye reviewed it in March 2026 and singled out the meze, among them a borani of feta, roasted pepper and truffle oil, and a smoky mutabbel.

set.hook: Ahmet Usta's hand-chopped kebabs at a Maslak grill counter, now a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand.
set.why: Ahmet Usta has worked the grill for about 20 years, and you can sit close enough to watch him chop the meat by hand before it goes over the coals. Fatih Tutak compares the scene to Japanese robatayaki: one cook, one fire. MICHELIN lists the house as a Bib Gourmand, and Time Out points to the Adana kebab, the small çöp şiş skewers and a pistachio baklava to finish. Book for lunch and after office hours, when Maslak's towers empty into the room.

set.hook: Kenan and Pınar Çetinkaya's twelve-seat fire counter in Kadıköy, one MICHELIN Star since December 2025.
set.why: Kenan Çetinkaya and Pınar Korgan Çetinkaya run Araf together: twelve seats around one open fire, in a residential block in 19 Mayıs rather than on a dining street. set.hook: Musa Dağdeviren's Kadıköy market lokanta, cooking recipes gathered from villages across Anatolia.
set.why: Dağdeviren, born in Nizip near Gaziantep, opened his first Çiya on Güneşlibahçe Sokak in 1987 and the Sofrası a decade later. He travels to record recipes before they vanish, and the counter changes daily with the season and what arrives from his suppliers. Netflix's Chef's Table gave him an episode. Point at the pots, ask what is new today, and expect dishes you will not meet at the next lokanta.

set.hook: Antakya cooking from a brick oven on Akarsu Yokuşu in Cihangir, open from breakfast until 02:00.
set.why: The kitchen cooks Hatay's dishes with a light modern hand, and many of them come out of a brick oven: lahmacun, and roasted peppers crushed with walnuts and pomegranate molasses, as MICHELIN's inspectors note. The guide added it to its Bib Gourmand list in the 2026 Türkiye edition and praised the service at breakfast, lunch and dinner alike. Antakya's food has carried extra weight since the 2023 earthquakes destroyed much of the old city.

set.hook: The Cihangir breakfast room that brought Van's herb cheese, murtuğa and kavut to Istanbul.
set.why: In Van, breakfast is the main event of the day, and this room on Defterdar Yokuşu has served it to Istanbul since around 2004. Order otlu peynir, the Van cheese cured with wild herbs; murtuğa, flour and egg scrambled in butter; and kavut, roasted grain sweetened with honey and walnuts. A May 2026 listing puts the average near 500 lira a head. There are no bookings, and the small room fills at weekends.

set.hook: A breakfast salon on Beşiktaş's Çelebioğlu Sokak, known for Erzincan kavurma, menemen and bal kaymak.

set.hook: Sütiş's Emirgan branch on the Bosphorus shore, where breakfast is built around its own kaymak.
set.why: Sütiş began as Mevlüt Kocadağ's dairy shop in Nişantaşı in 1953, and the Emirgan waterfront branch opened in 1986. Time Out notes that the kaymak and kaşar are the company's own, and that the Ezine cheese comes from a farm producing only for Sütiş. set.hook: Siirt-style büryan lamb, slow-cooked in a pit over coals, a few steps from the Valens Aqueduct.
set.why: Büryan is a side of young lamb lowered into a deep pit over coals and left until the meat falls apart under a thin layer of crisp fat. The Avcı family from Siirt claim the trade since 1892, and an usta still slices from the sides hanging on hooks and serves the meat on flatbread with only salt. Order perde pilavı too, rice baked inside a pastry dome, and come by lunchtime.

set.hook: A Black Sea lokanta off İstiklal: Laz stews, cornbread and anchovy pilaf ladled from a line of pots.
set.why: Hızır Keskin opened Hayvore in 2009, naming it with the Laz word for 'I am here'. The counter holds more than twenty stewed dishes, and the Black Sea staples are the order: hamsili pilav, rice baked under anchovies; kuymak, a cornmeal and cheese fondue; cornbread, Çayeli dry beans and stuffed collard leaves. Gault&Millau Türkiye gave it one toque in its 2026 guide, unusual for a room where most plates cost a few hundred lira.

set.cosign: Gault&Millau Türkiye 2026 - one toque; Culinary Backstreets, 'Hayvore: Lost and Found'
set.person: Hızır Keskin, founder - ran the Black Sea house Sisore ('where are you?' in Laz) before opening Hayvore in 2009. Two 2026 directory listings name Ayşe Banu Tağcı as executive chef. A second Hayvore (Lokanta Hayvore) runs at Galataport.

set.hook: Damascus home cooking on Akşemsettin Caddesi in Fatih, every dish tuned to the owner's mother's taste.
set.why: Bilal Khalaf traded computers in Syria until the war closed his shops in 2013. In Fatih he set out to serve the food of a Damascus home, and tasted each dish with his mother for a month before calling it right. Order the dishes cooked in hot yogurt, shakriyeh and kibbeh labaniyyeh, or the meat baked in clay pots. The room serves no alcohol and keeps long hours, roughly 08:30 to 23:30.
set.hours: Daily 08:30-23:30 per a directory listing - unconfirmed by the house

saruja.evidence: Building Markets business listing (undated): owner Bilal Khalaf, Syrian home cooking, Fatih (Akşemsettin Cad. 31/A) and Başakşehir branches, Sun-Sat 08:30-23:30, dishes including meat in pottery pots and safiha. No 2026-dated item found, so statusChecked kept. Search extracts only.

set.hook: A round-the-clock tripe soup house on Tarlabaşı Bulvarı, ladling since 1960.
set.why: Lale has served işkembe, tripe soup, since 1960 and still does not close. Time Out calls it a Beyoğlu classic for tripe lovers that pulls in the late-night crowd and the early-morning workers alike, often at the same table. The house names Arif Sarı as its chef. If tripe is a step too far, kuzu paça, a soup of lamb trotters, comes from the same pots and is the gentler way in.

lale-iskembecisi.evidence: Time Out Istanbul entry (undated): open 7 days, 24 hours, Tarlabaşı Bulvarı 3. Trip.com listing: Şehit Muhtar, Tarlabaşı Blv. No:5, open all day, phone +90 212 252 69 69 (matches record). No 2026-dated item found, so statusChecked kept. Search extracts only.

set.hook: Ali Bulut's Samatya soup counter, serving kelle paça from the afternoon until about 03:00.
set.why: Ali Bulut, born in Trabzon and raised in Samatya, opened Mimoza as a meyhane in 1981; today it serves the soup the meyhane crowd ends its night with. The speciality is kelle paça, lamb head and trotters simmered for hours, finished with melted butter and a garlic-lemon sauce over the meat at the bottom of the bowl. Every bowl comes with a seasonal salad, and reviewers praise the low prices and the clean room.

tarihi-mimoza-corbacisi.evidence: Culinary Backstreets (Nov 2025, already on record) via tag page; Wanderlog reviews describing kelle paça with butter and garlic-lemon sauce, friendly service, low prices, cleanliness. No 2026-dated item found, so statusChecked kept. Search extracts only.

set.hook: A century-old Beyoğlu name on Sahne Sokak, relaunched in 2024 as an Adana kebab and meze grill.
set.why: For more than a hundred years Degustasyon was a Beyoğlu fixture, first run by Italians and later a haunt of the young republic's writers. After a short, unhappy spell as a showy tourist steakhouse it was relaunched in fall 2024 under Mehmet Tanrıkulu, an Adana-born usta not yet thirty. Culinary Backstreets went back in March 2026 and rated it among Beyoğlu's strongest addresses for Adana kebab and meze.

tarihi-degustasyon-ocakbasi.evidence: Search for 2026 coverage returned nothing new; the Culinary Backstreets article of 6 March 2026 already on record remains the latest dated source. statusChecked kept. Search extracts only.

set.hook: Rice-stuffed mussels at the Beşiktaş shop that grew from a boy's street stand into a chain.
set.why: Ahmet began selling stuffed mussels as a child outside Istanbul schools, after his family moved from İzmir when he was two. He opened this Beşiktaş shop in 2014, and Culture Trip reported it selling up to 80,000 mussels a day. Each shell holds spiced rice cooked inside it; you squeeze on lemon and keep eating until you tell the counter to stop. Branches now run across Turkey and abroad, but this is the first.

set.hook: Macedonian-style kokoreç wound with lamb sweetbreads, from a family spit begun in 1968; book first.
set.why: Ali Sayı came to Istanbul from Bingöl and in 1968 began grilling kokoreç beside his uncle in the Çiçek Pasajı, later opening his own place in Dolapdere. His son Oğuzhan carries it on. The style is Macedonian: lamb intestine wrapped double and wound with uykuluk, sweetbreads. Output is limited each day, so the shop works by reservation only, and its open days shift when it travels to food festivals.
set.hours: Not published by the house. One guide gives Tuesday-Saturday 11:00-21:00; another says open days vary with the festivals it attends - reserve and confirm by phone or Instagram

set.hook: The Taksim büfe behind the ıslak burger: small buns soaked in garlicky tomato sauce, served late.
set.why: The business was set up on Taksim Square in 1972, and the Kızılkaya family put their name on it six years later. It claims both the first et döner of any Taksim büfe and the invention of the ıslak hamburger: a small patty in a soft bun soaked in garlicky tomato sauce, then held in a glass steam cabinet until it softens. It stays open late, so the queue forms when İstiklal empties.

set.hook: Balat's 1890 meyhane, opened by a Rum sea captain, now cooking some sixty mezes under chef Ahmet Arı.
set.why: Asteri Dulidis, a Rum sea captain, opened the meyhane in 1890, and his family kept it until 2001. It burned in 1955 and was rebuilt on the same walls. Chef Ahmet Arı joined in 2013 and builds the meze table from Middle Eastern, Cretan, Greek and old Istanbul recipes, made fresh each day. Gault&Millau Türkiye gave it one toque in its 2026 guide. Sources disagree on who owns it today.
set.hours: Daily, lunch into late evening; listings disagree (12:00-01:00 in a June 2026 directory, 13:00-24:00, or to 22:00 per an older Time Out page) - call ahead (+90 546 631 21 30)

set.hook: Kadıköy's family lokanta since 1919, by the fish market, with well over a hundred dishes a day.
set.why: Fehmi Efendi's family came from Yanya, today Ioannina in Greece, and he opened the lokanta in 1919; the third generation still runs it. Earlier branches elsewhere have closed, so the three-storey building where the street drops to the Kadıköy fish market is the only one left. Order papaz yahnisi, a garlicky meat stew, iç pilav, and elbasan tava, lamb baked under a yogurt crust. MICHELIN lists it as a Bib Gourmand.

set.hook: The Gaziantep kebab family's first Istanbul house in Samatya, birthplace of the pistachio kebab.
set.why: The family took up kebab-making in Gaziantep in 1912, and Arif Develi opened in Samatya in 1966. He is credited with the fıstıklı kebap, lamb mince worked through with Antep pistachio, still the most ordered dish in the house. Pistachios, pepper paste and bulgur come up from Gaziantep, and the house says it uses only milk-fed lamb. In 2006 The Observer put Develi on its list of the world's 100 best restaurants.

develi-samatya.evidence: Istanbul.com kebab guide, Time Out (TR), yemek.com Samatya round-up, Timetürk (2014, '102-year-old Turkish giant'): 1912 origin, Samatya 1966, pistachio kebab credited to Arif Develi, ingredients from Gaziantep, Observer top-100 in 2006. One source says Arif Develi came to Istanbul in 1962 (conflict). One undated article says Arif Develi died 'last October' and his sons now run it - not verified. No 2026-dated item found, so statusChecked kept. Search extracts only.
